sections.html:
Pope County's seat and biggest city, Russellville, lies where the Ozarks begin, just north of the Arkansas River. In 2020 it held 28,940 people in 10,958 households, and the 2025 figure is estimated at 29,521. Pope County had 63,381 residents in 2020.

Manufacturing, Arkansas Nuclear One, Arkansas Tech University and Lake Dardanelle anchor local demand. People who take a job with one of those employers, or leave one, often have to move quickly, and an as-is sale is one way to meet a tight date.

Lake Dardanelle is a reservoir created by a dam finished in 1965, and the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System runs through the area. Value on the water depends heavily on the specific lot, so a buyer will want to see the FEMA flood map for your address.

Rain peaks in April and May, at 4.83 and 4.67 inches, and that is when leaky roofs, clogged gutters and soggy yards reveal themselves. Summer is hot, with July highs near 92 degrees, so a buyer is likely to ask about the cooling system's age.

Russellville code enforcement covers property maintenance, vegetation, building violations, zoning violations and sign violations. A concern can be reported by phone, at the counter or on the online Code Enforcement Requests portal, and an officer then visits the property.

  • No violation found: the case is closed.
  • Violation confirmed: a Notice of Violation goes by mail to the owner, and also to the property when that address is different.
  • The owner can fix the problem or submit a plan of repair to ask for more time.
  • If the violation remains, the city may issue civil penalties or pursue abatement.

Got a notice on a house you just inherited? Reply fast with a plan of repair. The other option is selling as-is to a buyer willing to do the work.

If you think a value is off, begin with the assessor, whose office sets real property values at market level using comparable sales.

Violation letters are mailed to the owner and, if different, to the property. An owner far away can miss the first one when the mailing address on file is outdated. Heirs and distant landlords should correct their address with the county and have someone check the mail at the house.

Make a plan of repair specific. Name the fixes, the person doing them and the finish date, and hand it to the officer in writing. The officer can re-inspect after the date you give. If the problem is still there, civil penalties or abatement follow, so selling before that point keeps costs down.

Tax books open March 1 and close October 15, and penalties are added after that date. When October 15 lands on a weekend or a post office holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

Arkansas taxes are paid one year in arrears, so a real estate bill goes to the owner of record on January 1 of the previous year. If the house sells during the year, the closing documents say whether buyer or seller owes the bill. With an escrow account, the lender gets the statement only if you ask in writing, so request your own copy if you want one.

Two straight years of unpaid real estate tax send the land to the Commissioner of State Lands. It remains with the state for two years, then goes to auction. Clearing the balance before certification keeps every option open, including a normal sale.

If a balance is open, work in this order:

  • Get the full amount owed from the collector.
  • Give that number to the title company and to the buyer.
  • Make sure the payoff appears on the closing statement, so it comes out of your proceeds.
  • File the paid receipt with your closing papers.

When a deed is recorded in Arkansas, a transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 is paid by stamp. Decide in the contract who buys it.

No Arkansas rule forces every seller to list known defects, and the Seller Property Disclosure form is encouraged but optional. A leak, a cracked slab or a worn-out cooling system is better admitted up front than argued about after closing.

An inherited house adds a few steps. The deed or estate papers must show who can sign, the tax status should be checked right away, and any city notice should be answered while the estate is sorted out. A buyer paying cash can often close faster than a buyer who needs a mortgage, which matters when taxes keep coming due while the house sits empty.

sections.h2: Questions to ask before you list
sections.html:
A few answers will shape every offer you get, so settle them first.

  • Does the house sit near the lake or river, and has anyone checked its flood map status?
  • Is there an open city notice, and has a plan of repair been filed?
  • Is this year's tax bill paid, and who is responsible for it at closing?
  • Does anyone besides you need to sign?

With those four answered, you can compare a cash offer against a listing on equal terms, and a buyer has little left to question.

The steps run in about the same order however you sell.

  1. You gather the deed, the tax statement and any city notice.
  2. The buyer reviews the house and the papers and makes a written offer.
  3. A title company searches the records for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You agree on a closing date and who pays each fee.
  5. At closing, the deed is signed and recorded and you receive the proceeds.

Delays almost always come from paper: a lien nobody mentioned, a tax bill that fell behind, or an heir who has not signed. Dig those up early and closing goes smoothly.

Selling for cash skips the repair list, the showings and the lender's appraisal. It suits a house under a code notice, an estate property, or a seller on a deadline.

Bring these to the first conversation:

  • The deed, or court papers showing your authority to sign.
  • The latest Pope County tax statement.
  • Any Notice of Violation and your plan of repair.
  • A payoff statement if a mortgage remains.

A title company runs the closing. It pays liens and taxes out of the proceeds and has the deed recorded.

faqs.q: How many people live in Russellville?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 28,940 and the 2025 estimate is 29,521. Pope County had 63,381 residents in 2020.

faqs.q: When are Pope County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The tax books open March 1 and close October 15, and penalties are added afterward. If the date falls on a weekend or post office holiday, payment is due the next business day.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax when a Russellville house sells?
faqs.a: Whatever the closing documents say. Bills are issued to the January 1 owner of record from the prior year, since Arkansas collects a year behind.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore a Russellville code violation notice?
faqs.a: Civil penalties or abatement can follow a re-inspection. Submitting a plan of repair to the officer can buy you more time.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Russellville house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, and sooner is better. Two consecutive unpaid years can lead to certification to the Commissioner of State Lands, so settle the balance before that.
